chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Dawood al-Raqqi, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Among My believing servants are servants whose affairs of their religion cannot be rectified for them except through wealth, abundance, and health in the body. So I test them with wealth, abundance, and health of the body, so that I may rectify their religious affairs for them.'

And among My believing servants are servants whose affairs of their religion cannot be rectified for them except through poverty, destitution, and sickness in their bodies. So I test them with poverty, destitution, and sickness, so that I may rectify their religious affairs for them. And I am the One Who knows best what rectifies the religious affairs of My believing servants.

And among My believing servants is one who strives in My worship, rising from his sleep and the pleasure of his pillow, staying awake for Me through the nights, thus tiring himself in My worship. So I strike him with drowsiness for the night and the two nights, as a consideration from Me to him and a preservation for him, so he sleeps until morning. Then he rises, and he is disgusted with himself, fretting over it.

And if I were to leave him alone to do what he intends from My worship, self-conceit would enter him because of that. So self-conceit would lead him to trial through his deeds, and there would come to him from that that which causes his destruction due to his conceit in his deeds and his satisfaction with himself, until he thinks that he has surpassed the worshippers and exceeded the limit of deficiency in his worship. Thus, he becomes distant from Me at that time, while he thinks he is drawing near to Me.

So let the workers not rely upon their deeds which they perform for My reward. For if they strive and tire themselves and spend their lives in My worship, they would be deficient, not reaching the full measure of their worship in what they seek from Me of My generosity, the bliss in My Paradise, and the high ranks in My vicinity. But (they attain it) by My Mercy.

So let them have trust in My grace, let them rejoice, and let them be assured in their good opinion of Me. For My Mercy will overtake them at that time, and from Me, My Pleasure will reach them, and My Forgiveness will clothe them in My Pardoning. Indeed, I am Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful, and with that I am Named.'
ai.seo_question: How does Allah test believers with wealth versus poverty, and why does He strike worshippers with drowsiness?
ai.summary: This Hadith Qudsi, recorded in al-Kafi, elucidates the divine wisdom behind varying states of wealth, health, and fatigue, framing them as precise instruments for spiritual refinement rather than arbitrary trials. It highlights the subtle danger of 'al-'ujb' (self-conceit) in diligent worshipers, illustrating how Allah’s mercy often manifests through interruption or ease to preserve humility. The narration concludes by anchoring ultimate salvation in divine grace (rahmah) rather than the sheer volume of deeds, a core tenet of Shia theological optimism regarding God's boundless generosity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Dawood Al Raqqy, from Abu Ubeyda Al Haza’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said: “From My<sup>azwj</sup> believing servants there are servants whose matters of their Religion cannot be correct for them except with the richness and the capacity, and the health in the body. Therefore, I<sup>azwj</sup> Test them with the riches, and the capacity, and the health of the body in order to Correct upon them the matter of their Religion.

And from My<sup>azwj</sup> believing servants are such servants that the matter of their Religion cannot be correct for them except with the destitution, and the poverty, and the sickness in their bodies. Therefore, I<sup>azwj</sup> Test then with the destitution, and the poverty, and the sickness, in order to Correct upon them the matter of their Religion. And I<sup>azwj</sup> am more Knowing with what is correct upon him in the matter of the Religion of My<sup>azwj</sup> believing servant.

And that, from Myazwj believing servants is the one who strive in Myazwj worship. So he is standing from his mattress and the pleasure of his pillow, and he spends the night in praying Salāt to Meazwj, thus tiring himself in Myazwj worship. So Iazwj Strike him with the drowsiness for the night and the two nights, as a Consideration from Meazwj to him, whether he would remain upon it. But he goes to sleep until the morning. Then he arises, and he is disgusted with himself, upset over it.

And if I<sup>azwj</sup> were to Leave him alone, between him and what he wants from My<sup>azwj</sup> worship, the self-conceit would enter into him due to that, so he would become self-conceited to the strife by his deed, and there would come to him from that what has destruction in it due to his self-conceitedness by his deeds, and satisfaction from himself, until he would think that he has surpassed the (other) worshippers and has exceeded in My<sup>azwj</sup> worship, the limit of deficiency. Thus, he would be remote from Me<sup>azwj</sup> during that, and he would be thinking that he has come nearer to Me<sup>azwj</sup>.

Thus, the workers should not be reliant upon their deeds which they are performing for My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Rewards. If they were to strive and exhaust themselves and finish off their lifetime in My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> worship, they would be deficient ones without having reach in My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> worship, that which My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> worship should happen to be regarding what they are seeking from My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Benevolence and the Bounties in My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Paradise, and the highest of My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> lofty Levels in My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> vicinity, but (they should be relying upon) My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mercy.

So let them be trusting in My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Grace, so let they be happy and have good thoughts with Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, for in My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mercy would come to them during that, and from Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Pleasure would reach them, and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Forgiveness clothing them in My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Pardoning. So I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> am Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, the Beneficent, the Merciful, and with that I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> am Named’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from Dawud al-Riqqiy from ‘Ubayda al-Hadhdha’ from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said that Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, ‘Among My believing servants there are those whose religious lives can only be at their best with wealth, comfort and good health. I try them by means of wealth, comfort and good health and this makes their religious affairs to be in the best condition.

Also among My believing servants there are those whose religious lives are only at their best with poverty, destitution and ailing health. I try them by means of poverty, destitution and ailing health and this helps their religious lives to be in the best condition. I know what is good for the religious matters of my believing servants.

Among My believing servants there are those who strive to worship Me. They wake up from sleep leaving their comfortable pillow for Tahajjud (special prayer at night). They experiences fatigue and I allow slumber overcome them on one or two nights, a trial from Me to see if he continues, he goes to sleep and wakes up upset and angry over his own self.

If I allow him to do the way he wants to worship, he may develop a sense of conceit (unwanted pride) that can lead him to mischief in his deeds. This may bring about his destruction. It can so happen due to his happiness with whatever his soul desires. He may begin to feel as if he has excelled all worshippers and has surpassed the limits of defective worship. In so doing he moves away from Me even though he thinks that he is getting closer to Me.

Therefore, they must not rely on their good deeds that they do to receive rewards from Me. Even if they strive hard, tire themselves and finish their lives worshipping Me they fall short, in worshipping Me truly, in their quest for My generous rewards, My bounties in paradise and high positions near Me.

They must only trust in My mercy, be happy with My generosity and always be hopeful about Me. In such cases My mercy will reach them as well as my approval and forgiveness and my pardon will provide them cover; I am Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful, and thus 1 have taken such names.’”
